Flow Metrics · Charlie’s Epic Flow Clinic

Welcome to Flow Metrics

A flow clinic for your delivery teams: give it your work items — a completed date, a start date and a type — and it works out throughput, cycle and lead time, work in progress, and the age of everything still open, grouped into Flow, Delivery and Health, for one team or across all of them.

Everything you enter stays in this browser. Nothing is uploaded — there is no account and no server.

Start Fresh opens Your Data, where you paste a report out of Jira or add work items one at a time — a board kept by hand works just as well.

Load Sample Data fills every chart with three invented teams and nine months of work items, each team named for the one thing it shows, so you can see what the app does before typing anything of your own. The figures are made up.

Restore a Backup reads a Flow Metrics export.

Forecast Ahead is for a team that has not started. You type how fast you think it will go and it answers the same two questions it would answer from real data — when a scope finishes, and how much finishes by a date. It is your estimate with the arithmetic done, not a measurement.

Every Team, Side by Side

Press a column heading to sort by it. Press a team's name to open its dashboard. Every row is read over the same window and as of the same date, whatever each team's own export runs to — the Data to column says which teams are behind.

Paste Work Items for This Team

Needs a completed date, a start date and a work type somewhere in each row. Paste the export as it comes — the right columns are worked out from the data and named back to you below, and anything else is read for those and thrown away. Tabs and commas both work — so does a single space, where it leaves a column of dates behind — and a header row is skipped. An issue key column like DAE-1552 is picked up if there is one, and it names the dots on the charts. One export covering several teams goes in through Paste several teams instead, which splits it by the project id at the front of each key. Items that are started but not finished belong here too: they count as work started. A created date is optional and adds lead time.

Loaded Data

Press an item to edit it, or add one by hand. A row pasted from an export and a row typed in here are the same thing once they are saved — both go through the same checks, and both are yours to correct.

Clean Up Old Data

Work items pile up, and years of them make every paste and every backup heavier without telling you anything new. This drops the ones older than a cutoff you pick. You choose how far back to keep, and see exactly what would go, before anything is deleted.

No Data Yet

Head to the Your Data tab and paste your work items — a completed date, a start date and a type. Add a created date too and you get lead time as well. No Jira export to hand? Add a Work Item on that same tab asks for the same things one item at a time, stage times included:

No Features on This Team

Lead time needs a Created date — how long work takes from being raised, not just from being started. Add a Created column to your paste, or fill in the Created box on an item.

A feature counts only when it is finished — a period whose pace runs out halfway through one has delivered the ones before it, which is why a wider range here moves the answer more than it looks like it should.

For a team with no history to resample. A typed range spreads less than real periods do — it has no quiet weeks and no spikes in it — so treat its confidence as the most generous reading, not the safest one. The team setting above is switched off while this is on: multiplying a guess by a guess compounds two people’s pessimism.

↗ Sprint Predictability

Find

Your teams, the trains they are on, your workflow stages and the aliases they match — and any work item, by its issue key or its type. An item opens straight into its editor.

Teams, ARTs & Stages

Teams

Each team keeps its own work items. The picker in the header chooses which one the dashboard is showing; Settings are shared by all of them.

Project id is the letters at the front of the team's issue keys — DAE for DAE-1552. It is what lets one export covering several teams be pasted in one go and split between them; it changes no figure. Leave it blank and the team simply takes nothing from a split.

WIP ≤ is how much work this team means to have open at once, and 85% ≤ how long it means an item to take — the promise the 85th percentile is read against. Both are drawn as a line on the charts and neither changes a figure: they are what the figures are compared to. Leave either blank and the app states the number without judging it, which is what it does today.

85% ≤ is about work that has FINISHED — it is checked against the items this team delivered. The separate ageing threshold in Settings is about work that has not: how long something can sit open before it is flagged. They are different questions, so they are usually different numbers — and the threshold is normally the lower of the two, because an item that has already passed your target is too late to rescue. A promise of 10 days is often watched with a threshold around 6.

Agile Release Trains

An Agile Release Train groups teams together. It is a label only — every figure is still worked out per team — and All Teams gains a picker for it. Teams need not be on one.

Statuses

Every status this app has read out of your exports, and the only words from a work system it keeps. Delete any you do not want; the items in it keep their dates and simply stop being grouped. The list holds at most 40.

Workflow Stages

A stage is a part of your workflow you want to measure the wait in — Build, Review, Test. Paste a Time in Status export with a column per status and each item's days land in the stage you have matched that status to. Several statuses can feed one stage: list them all and their days are added together. No export? Every stage you add here also gets a box on the work item form, so the days can simply be typed in.

The statuses come out of your export; the stages are yours. Paste an export with a Status column and the statuses in it are added to your list above, where you can see them and delete any you do not want. Grouping them into stages is optional — the work item age chart draws by status on its own — and a stage is worth adding when several statuses are really one part of your workflow, or when you want them in your own order. Change a grouping and every item you have already pasted moves with it; nothing needs re-pasting.

Ticking a status is enough. A status you have ticked into a stage also claims that status's column in a Time in Status export — so one tick does both jobs, and a set-up made by ticking needs nothing typed. The status names box is for what ticking cannot reach: a status that is not in your list yet because no export has shown it to this app, and an old spelling your board has since renamed. Type those exactly as Jira spells them; capitals and punctuation don't matter, and a typed name wins where it disagrees with a tick.

Type the status, not the whole heading. A real export heads these columns Days in Code Review or Time in Code Review; the words in front are read off and the status inside is what has to match, so Code Review is the alias to type. It is also the spelling that matches a plain export's Status column, which the long one cannot. Leave Days in Done and Days Blocked out. The first keeps growing after the work has finished, and the second runs at the same time as whatever status the item is really in — neither is time spent in a stage.

Settings

Everything the charts depend on is here, and nothing else — a setting that changes nothing is worse than a missing one. Every one of them is shared by every team; the two figures a team sets for ITSELF are on its own row under Teams & Stages.

Labels & Work Types

The words on the charts, and what counts as a defect.

Unfinished work only — nothing that has completed is ever counted here. Not the same as a team’s 85% ≤ target, which is checked against work that has finished; set each lower than that target so something is flagged while there is still time to act on it.

The feature box is empty by default, and empty is off — a fortnight is a rule about work items, and nothing here assumes it holds for features. Until you set a number, the Aged Work card in the feature view says so and shows what that team’s finished features actually took, so the number you pick is measured against your own board.

Separate them with commas, exactly as they appear in your Type column. Rows matching are kept apart from your work items, so no item-level figure moves. Empty is off — nothing ships here by default, because a guess at somebody else’s board is a setting that matches nothing. Pair it with a Parent key column to join items to the features they belong to.

Cycle time, lead time and the ageing threshold skip weekends — an item started on a Friday and finished on the Monday takes one day, not three. Public holidays are not known to this app and still count as working days, wherever you are.

An ignored item still counts as delivered — throughput, net flow, the cumulative flow diagram, work in progress and the defect rate do not move. Only its cycle time, lead time and time in stage stop counting. Work that is still in progress is never ignored, however long it has been open, so the aged work figures are untouched.

Automatically ignores anything more than three interquartile ranges above the upper quartile of what finished in the window on screen — the standard test for an extreme outlier — and needs at least 12 finished items before it will offer an opinion. Narrowing the date picker changes what counts, because an outlier is only unusual next to the work beside it.

Most boards should leave this off. The median and 85% figures this dashboard leads with already shrug off a long tail — if one enormous item is spoiling the picture, the average is the only figure it is spoiling, and the median beside it is the better number to read.
Anything whose Type is blank, or doesn't match the defect text above, counts as ordinary planned work.
Work Type Filter List

The choices in the Work Type filter on the dashboard. Display is what you pick; Value is the text matched against your Type column. Put several types in one row by separating them with commas — Story, Task is one choice covering both. Each is matched exactly, so Task does not pull in Sub-task. The arrows set the order the choices appear in the picker. Leave the All row alone — it means "no filter", which is why it is greyed out.

DisplayValue Actions

Paste Several Teams at Once

One export covering more than one team, split by the project id at the front of each issue key — DAE-1552 goes to whichever team is set to DAE. It is read once, as one export, so every team is read the same way. Nothing is written until you press one of the load buttons, and a team this paste does not name is never touched.

Back Up & Restore

One JSON file holding every team, their work items and your shared settings — a copy you keep, independent of this browser. It is the only copy of your data that exists anywhere else, so it is worth taking one.

Restoring replaces every team in this browser. You'll see what the file holds and be asked to confirm first. A backup file is also how you move your data to another device — download it here, and restore it there.

Start Again

Deletes every team and every work item in this browser. Your settings and your theme are kept.

Add a Work Item

An item needs at least one of those two. Leave Completed empty for work still in progress — it still counts as work started.

Days in Each Stage (optional)

Calendar days, counted the way a Time in Status export counts them — the working-days setting does not apply here. Leave a box empty if you do not have that figure; an empty box is left out altogether, where a 0 says the item crossed that stage inside a day.

Clean Up Old Data

Choose how much history to keep. Nothing goes until you press Remove items — the summary below only says what that press would do.

How Much to Keep

Months count back from the newest item in the data, not from today — the same anchor the dashboard's date window uses, so a stale export is never one press from vanishing.

Which Teams
Unfinished Items

Off by default: an item with no completion date is still in progress, however old its start date.

Share a Read-Only Link

Anyone opening this link sees the figures you pick, with no way to change them and no sign-in. The data travels inside the link itself — it isn't uploaded anywhere, and it doesn't touch whatever they have saved in their own browser.

Which Teams
How Much History

Nothing is deleted — this only decides how much of your history rides in the link, which is what makes a long history shareable. Months count back from the newest item in the data, the same anchor the clean-up tool uses.

Unfinished Items

Off by default: an item with no completion date is still in progress, so it belongs on the charts however old its start is.

Your Link

If your paste had an issue key column, those keys travel in the link — they are what names the items on the charts, and a link without them would show a different picture from yours. Nothing else out of your work system does: no summaries, no statuses, no names.

This is a snapshot, frozen as it looks right now — later edits won't appear, so send a fresh link when the numbers move. There's no way to withdraw one once sent, so treat it like emailing a spreadsheet. If you trimmed the history, whoever opens it is told which date the copy starts from.
